name: Sogdian Camel Raiders

abilities.name: Frenzy
abilities.text: Improves a unit's attack capabilities for an extended period of time.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

attributes.name: Campaign Stealth
attributes.text: This unit can move around the campaign map without being seen.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Ignore Terrain
attributes.text: Speed penalties caused by the terrain are ignored by this unit.

attributes.name: Raider
attributes.text: This unit may set buildings on fire, cause more fire damage with torches and capture faster than other units.

attributes.name: Resistant to Heat
attributes.text: This unit tires less quickly in the desert.

attributes.name: Scare (horses)
attributes.text: This unit gives a morale penalty to enemy horses.

short: Sogdians are keen in the ways of war; a camel is but another weapon.
history: Sogdia was once a belligerent power to the north of Persia, independent buffer between the Archaemenids and the nomadic Scythians. That all changed, however, after Alexander the Great conquered the Sogdian Rock and merged the territory with Baktria, shattering the military power of both in the process. After subjugation by Alexander, Sogdians became traders, cementing themselves far along the Silk Road. In approximately AD260, the Sogdian central city, Samarkand, was conquered by the Sassanid Empire, following which it became a major religious centre, spreading Manichaeism into Asia. Sogdia's independent military power was forever dismantled but the Sassanids held on to Sogdia until the mid-4th century, when the nomadic confederation of Hephtalites seized the region.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
